title: Container Images and Container Commands

header.html: Define, build and modify container images
Kubernetes v1.37.0 (3-node test cluster, containerd 2.3.4); images built with Docker 29

toc.title: From a Dockerfile to a running container
Using an image in a Pod
Container commands: ENTRYPOINT, CMD, command and args

html:
1From a Dockerfile to a running container

A container image is a read-only package: a file system plus the default command to run. You describe it in a Dockerfile, build it with a tool (docker build or podman build), and either keep it on the machine, save it as a file, or push it to a registry. A Pod names the image; the kubelet on the node pulls it and starts the container.

The Dockerfile lines: building the image

Dockerfile line What it does Example
FROM the base image; always the first real line FROM busybox:1.36
RUN run a command while building; makes a new layer RUN apk add --no-cache curl
COPY copy files from the build folder into the image COPY app.conf /etc/app.conf
WORKDIR the working directory for later lines and for the container WORKDIR /app
ENV set an environment variable, kept at run time ENV GREETING=hello
ARG a build-time variable, not kept at run time ARG VERSION=1

The Dockerfile lines: metadata and the start command

Dockerfile line What it does Example
LABEL metadata on the image LABEL version=2
EXPOSE documents the port the app listens on (does not publish it) EXPOSE 8080
USER the user the container runs as USER 1000
ENTRYPOINT the program that always runs ENTRYPOINT ["echo"]
CMD the default arguments, or the default command if there is no ENTRYPOINT CMD ["hello"]

Layers, the build cache and multi-stage builds

Layers and the build cache. Each RUN, COPY and ADD line creates a layer. Docker reuses unchanged layers, so put the lines that change often (your code) at the bottom and the slow, stable ones (installing packages) at the top.

Exec form versus shell form. CMD ["sleep", "3600"] (a JSON array) starts the program directly. CMD sleep 3600 (a plain string) starts it through /bin/sh -c. Use the exec form, and use a shell (["sh", "-c", "echo $GREETING"]) only when you need variable expansion.

Multi-stage builds use several FROM lines: build in a large image, then COPY --from=build only the result into a small final image. The final image stays small and holds no compilers.

2Build, tag, run, save

cd ~/build/hello                    # the folder that holds the Dockerfile (the "build context")
docker build -t hello:1.0 .         # podman build -t hello:1.0 .  works the same
docker images                       # list local images
docker run --rm hello:1.0           # run once and remove the container
docker save hello:1.0 > hello.tar   # archive; podman: podman save -o hello.tar hello:1.0
docker load < hello.tar             # read it back on another machine
docker tag hello:1.0 registry.example.com/team/hello:1.0   # a second name
docker push registry.example.com/team/hello:1.0            # needs a registry and a login
Need Command
Build from another file name docker build -f Dockerfile.prod -t app:2 .
Pass a build argument docker build --build-arg VERSION=2 -t app:2 .
See the layers docker history hello:1.0
Read the labels and the command docker image inspect hello:1.0
Remove an image docker rmi hello:1.0

Names. An image name is registry/repository:tag, for example registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10. Without a registry the default is Docker Hub. Without a tag the tag is latest, which is a name, not a promise of the newest build: always give a real tag.

On the exam. The curriculum says "define, build and modify container images". The official pages read for this course do not say which tool is installed in the exam environment. Typical tasks edit a Dockerfile and build or save an image; if the tool is podman, the commands above are identical with podman instead of docker. Check which one exists (which podman docker) and read the task for the tag and the output file.

3Using an image in a Pod

A Pod references the image by name and tag. Two settings decide what the kubelet does:

Field Meaning
image name:tag, or name@sha256:... to pin an exact build
imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent (pull only if the node lacks the image), Always (check the registry every time), Never (never pull; the image must already be on the node)

The default is IfNotPresent, except when the tag is latest (or missing): then it is Always. That is why a local-only image tagged latest fails with ErrImagePull: the kubelet insists on asking a registry that does not have it. Fix it by setting imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent or Never, or use a real tag.

imagePullPolicy cannot be changed on a running Pod. Edit the YAML and recreate the Pod: kubectl get pod p -o yaml > p.yaml, change the field, then kubectl replace --force -f p.yaml.

Private registries. A Pod pulls from a private registry with imagePullSecrets, which names a Secret of type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (Module 9 shows how to create Secrets):

k create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.example.com --docker-username=dev --docker-password=pw
# in the Pod spec:  imagePullSecrets: [{name: regcred}]

4Container commands: ENTRYPOINT, CMD, command and args

The Pod's container can replace what the image runs:

Dockerfile Pod field Effect
ENTRYPOINT command the program to run
CMD args the arguments to the program

Rules: if you set command, the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD are ignored; if you set only args, the image's ENTRYPOINT stays and args replaces CMD; if you set neither, the image's defaults run.

containers:
- name: greeter
  image: busybox:1.36
  command: ["echo"]         # replaces ENTRYPOINT
  args: ["Hello CKAD"]      # replaces CMD

On the command line, everything after -- is the command and arguments: k run job1 --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never -- echo hello sets args to ["echo", "hello"] (and keeps the image ENTRYPOINT, which is empty for busybox, so it still runs). Add --command to put it into command instead: k run job1 --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never --command -- echo hello.

Environment variables go in env (name/value) and are visible to the process: k run web --image=nginx:alpine --env=MODE=prod. A value can also come from a ConfigMap or Secret (Module 9).

Exam tip

. The two most common image mistakes are the wrong tag (read the task twice) and latest with a local image. Verify with docker images (or podman images) after a build, and with k describe pod when a Pod will not start.

5Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m01 -->

Lab 1.1: build image

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-01-build-image)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The directory ~/build/hello contains a Dockerfile. Build an image from it and tag it hello:1.0. (Use docker build; on an exam host that has podman, the command is identical.)

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

cd ~/build/hello
docker build -t hello:1.0 .
docker run --rm hello:1.0

Lab 1.2: modify dockerfile

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-02-modify-dockerfile)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Dockerfile in ~/build/greeter builds an image that prints hello. Modify the Dockerfile so that the image prints hello team and carries the label version=2 (it now has version=1), then build it and tag it greeter:2.0.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

cd ~/build/greeter
sed -i 's/^LABEL version=1/LABEL version=2/; s/^ENV GREETING=hello/ENV GREETING="hello team"/' Dockerfile
cat Dockerfile
docker build -t greeter:2.0 .
docker run --rm greeter:2.0

Lab 1.3: save image archive

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-03-save-image-archive)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Build the image from the Dockerfile in ~/build/hello, tag it hello:3.0, and save it as an archive file ~/answers/hello-3.0.tar so that it can be loaded on another machine with docker load.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

cd ~/build/hello
docker build -t hello:3.0 .
docker save hello:3.0 > ~/answers/hello-3.0.tar
tar -tf ~/answers/hello-3.0.tar | head

Lab 1.4: local image pull policy

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-04-local-image-pull-policy)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace local, the Pod localapp uses the image ckad/app:latest. That image exists only in the local image store of the nodes (it is in no registry), and the Pod is stuck in ErrImagePull or ImagePullBackOff. Fix it so the Pod is Running with the same image and the kubelet does not pull the image from a registry. Keep the Pod name and namespace.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n local get pod localapp -o yaml | sed 's/imagePullPolicy: Always/imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent/' > /tmp/localapp.yaml
kubectl replace --force -f /tmp/localapp.yaml
kubectl -n local wait --for=condition=Ready pod/localapp --timeout=120s

Lab 1.5: command args

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-05-command-args)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace cmd, create a Pod named greeter with the image busybox:1.36 that runs the program echo with the single argument Hello CKAD, using the command and args fields of the container (not a shell string). The Pod must not restart after it finishes (restartPolicy: Never). Wait until it has completed.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n cmd run greeter --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/greeter.yaml
sed -i 's#^  - image: busybox:1.36#  - command: ["echo"]\n    args: ["Hello CKAD"]\n    image: busybox:1.36#' /tmp/greeter.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/greeter.yaml
kubectl -n cmd wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded pod/greeter --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cmd logs greeter

<!-- /LABS -->

6Recall questions

R1Which Dockerfile line sets the base image?

Show the answer

FROM.

R2Which command builds an image from the Dockerfile in the current folder and tags it hello:1.0?

Show the answer

docker build -t hello:1.0 . (or podman build -t hello:1.0 .).

R3How do you save an image to a file, and how do you load it again?

Show the answer

docker save hello:1.0 > hello.tar and docker load < hello.tar (podman: podman save -o, podman load -i).

R4What is the default imagePullPolicy for an image tagged latest?

Show the answer

Always; for any other tag it is IfNotPresent.

R5Which Pod field replaces the image's ENTRYPOINT, and which replaces its CMD?

Show the answer

command replaces ENTRYPOINT; args replaces CMD.

R6What does EXPOSE 8080 do?

Show the answer

It documents the port; it does not publish or open it.

R7Can you edit imagePullPolicy on a running Pod?

Show the answer

No; export the YAML, change it and recreate the Pod (kubectl replace --force -f).

R8Why use a multi-stage build?

Show the answer

To copy only the build result into a small final image without the build tools.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Dockerfile FROM, RUN, COPY, ENV, LABEL, EXPOSE, USER, ENTRYPOINT, CMD
Build docker build -t name:tag .; podman is identical
Save and load docker save name:tag > f.tar; docker load < f.tar
Pull policy default IfNotPresent; latest means Always; Never for local-only images
Command and args command = ENTRYPOINT, args = CMD; -- on kubectl run
Private registry imagePullSecrets with a docker-registry Secret
Immutable imagePullPolicy cannot change in place: replace --force
